text: Practice problem 1 October 11, 2025 Problem 1. If {v1, . . . , vk} is linearly independent and each vi ∈ Rn, what is the maximum possible value of k? Problem 2. Suppose v1, v2, v3 ∈ R4 are such that span(v1, v2, v3) = R4. Is this possible? Explain. Problem 3. If {v1, v2, v3} is a linearly dependent set in a vector space V , what can you say about dim span(v1, v2, v3)? Problem 4. Suppose v1, . . . , vn is a basis for a vector space V . Let w ∈ V . Under what conditions is the set {v1 + w, . . . , vn + w} linearly dependent? Prove your claim. Problem 5. (i) Show that sin x and sin 2x are linearly independent in C(R). (ii) Are the functions cos x and cos2 x linearly independent in C(R)? Justify your answer. Problem 6. Suppose V is finite-dimensional and dim dim V > 1. Prove that the set of noninvertible linear maps from V to itself is not a subspace of L(V, V ). Problem 7. If v1 + W, . . . , vm + W are linearly independent in V /W then v1, . . . , vm are linearly independent in V . Problem 8. If φ, ψ ∈ V ∗ are nonzero and ker φ = ker ψ. Show that φ, ψ are linearly dependent. Problem 9. Show that U +W is a direct sum if and only if there is an element v ∈ U +W such that the decomposition v = u + w for u ∈ U , w ∈ W is unique. Problem 10. Let V be finite dimensional and φ1, . . . , φm ∈ V ∗. Show that the following are equivalent: 1. φ1, . . . , φm are linearly independent 2. ⋂m i=1 ker φi has dimension dim V − m 3. There exists a basis v1, . . . , vn of V such that φi(vj) = δij for 1 ≤ i ≤ m, 1 ≤ j ≤ n 1 Problem 11. Suppose that v, x ∈ V and U, W are subspaces of V such that v + U = x + W . Prove that U = W . Problem 12. Suppose dim span(v1, . . . , vn) ≥ n. Show that v1, . . . , vn is linearly inde- pendent. Problem 13. Let v1, . . . , vk ∈ Rn. If k > n, show that the set v1, . . . , vk is linearly dependent. Problem 14. Let T : V → W , S : W → U be linear transformations. (i) Show that im(ST ) ⊂ im S and rank(ST ) ≤ rank(S). (ii)Show that im(T tSt) ⊂ im T t and rank(ST ) ≤ rank(T ). (iii) If R : U → X is linear. Show that rank(RST ) ≤ rank(S). Problem 15. We have seen in Lecture 1 that the set of all symmetric matrices V = {A ∈ Mn×n(R) : At = A} and anti-symmetric matrices W = {A ∈ Mn×n(R) : At = −A} are subspaces of Mn×n(R). (i) Find a basis of V and dim V . (ii) Find a basis of W and dim W . (iii) Show that Mn×n(R) = V ⊕ W . Hint: for any A ∈ Mn×n(R), write A = A+At 2 + A−At 2 . Problem 16. Find a matrix representing the linear transformation (i)  x1 x2 x3   ↦→    x1 + x2 + x3 x1 + x2 x3    . (ii)        x1 x2 ... xn−1 xn        ↦→        x2 x3 ... xn x1        . Problem 17. Let T : R3 → R3 be a linear transformation such that T vi = wi for i = 1, 2, 3, where v1 =   1 2 3   , v2 =   1 1 1   , v3 =  0 1 1   , and w1 =   1 0 1   , w2 =   0 3 1   , w3 =   2 1 0   . 2 (i) Find T   1 0 0  . (2) Find the 3 × 3 matrix [T ] β β with β = {v1, v2, v3}. Problem 18. True or False: There is a linear transformation T : R5 → R2 with kernel ker T = {(v1, . . . , v5) t ∈ R 5 : v1 = 3v2 and v3 = v4 = v5}. Justify your answer. Problem 19. Let D = d dt be the derivative operator. Let V be the real vector space spanned by the basis B = {1, t, et, e 2t, te 2t}. (1) Show that D is a linear map from V into itself. (2) Find the matrix M associated with D relative to the basis B. (3) Determine the rank of D. Problem 20. Let T : V → V be a linear transformation on a finite-dimensional vector space V . Let φ ∈ V ∗. (i) Define iφ : F → V ∗ by iφ(c) = cφ for c ∈ F . Show that im iφ = span(φ). (ii) We identify V with V ∗∗ by the natural isomorphism J and F ∗ with F by ℓ ↦→ ℓ(1) for ℓ ∈ F ∗. Show that under the identification above (iφ)t : V → F is given by (iφ)t(x) = φ(x) for x ∈ V . (iii) If ker T t = span(φ), then im T = ker φ. (iv) If im T t = span(φ), then ker T = ker φ. Hint: For (iii) (iv), you can use (i) (ii) combined with Theorem 6.15 proved in class. Problem 21. Let V = R4, and let W = span        1 0 1 0     ,     0 1 1 1        ⊆ V. Find a basis for the annihilator W ⊥ ⊆ V ∗, the set of all linear functionals φ : V → R such that φ(w) = 0 for all w ∈ W . Problem 22. Consider the linear system  a 1 1 1 a 1 1 1 1    x y z   =  b c 2   . (i) For which values of a, b, c does the system have a unique solution? (ii) For those values of a, b, c for which it has a non-unique solution, describe all solutions. 3 Problem 23. Consider the system of linear equations:    x + 3y + 2z + w = a, 2x + 5y + 3z = a, x − z = −b, y + z = b. (i) For what values of a and b does a solution of the system exist?
